I'm mapping out the grid components by color, noting the virus location at (4,5) and grouping connected cells of 4s, 8s, and 1s into separate clusters.

Checking the virus's reach with both adjacent 8-direction moves and jump moves over empty cells, I find it can reach the second 8-component through a jump at (4,7), infecting cells (1,8),(2,8),(3,8),(3,7),(4,7), and now I'm tracing further spread from those infected cells to their neighbors.

Continuing the jump checks from (3,8) and (4,7), everything stays uninfected except the one group. So only that single component (8b) ends up infected, while the virus component stays at 0 — giving a final answer of virus→0, 8b→2.

Checking the virus at (2,10), I trace its neighbors and jump moves, finding that (4,10) becomes infected since (3,10) is black—this connects to the "7" shaped piece spanning row 4 columns 7-11 and row 5 column 8, which gets infected as a result.

That "7" shape then spreads to (6,8), infecting the "4" shaped piece at row 6-7. I check jumps from that shape but they all land on empty or zero cells, so nothing further spreads. I also verify the "7" shape's own jump moves don't hit anything new.

So the final tally: both the "7" piece and the "4" piece get converted to infected (2), while the original virus cell becomes empty (0). I'm now writing out the updated grid row by row, starting with row 4.
